name: Oyindamola Kushimo
missingPieces: D1 omits three findings: unsalted MD5 (CWE-916), no JWT token expiry (CWE-613), and cookie missing Secure/SameSite (CWE-614). D2 chain is only three hops and omits stored XSS (02:18:47), open redirect (02:21:13), and the bulk-PII export step; the Hop 3 XXE verbatim PoC field is left blank.
feedback: D1 is well organised and the decoy work is the strongest part of the whole submission. You catalogued seven of the ten findings with correct OWASP classes, correct CWE numbers, and quoted lines for most, and your safe-construct verdict is exactly right: you named hash_equals, proved it is constant-time at the mechanism level, and correctly placed the real fault in the alg:none branch that bypasses it. Where D1 loses ground is the three findings you never wrote up: the unsalted MD5 hashing (CWE-916), the missing JWT token expiry (CWE-613), and the cookie lacking Secure and SameSite (CWE-614). Each missing finding costs its share, so seven of ten cannot earn near-full marks even with good quotes. In D2 your first two hops reconcile cleanly to the capture with verbatim proof, but the chain stops at three hops and skips the stored XSS at 02:18:47, the open redirect at 02:21:13, and the 312-row export as its own exfil step, and your Hop 3 XXE proof-of-concept field is simply blank where the 04-import-xxe.xml SYSTEM file:///etc/passwd payload should sit. Your SQLi CVSS is also off: you set A:H and scored 9.8, but the bypass does not affect availability, so the correct vector is CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N at about 9.1. The impact section is genuinely good, you extrapolated from the recovered sample, stated your per-user assumption, and landed on 312 customers and roughly 52.5M NGN tied to BoltCash, which is exactly the reasoning we wanted. D3 reads professionally: the executive summary is jargon-free and ends on the customers-and-naira headline, the threat model is concrete, the decoy is restated correctly, and the earliest-break fix (parameterise the login query to halt the chain at the first hop) is spot on. Your remediation table is risk-and-effort driven rather than pure CVSS, which is the right instinct, and your two detection stopgaps name specific fields, though the false-positive rates are described qualitatively (exceptionally low, low) rather than quantified. The findings section of D3 carries only three findings, which thins that row. D4 is solid: you answer all four prompts in your own voice, cite ISC2 Canon II by number as load-bearing, anchor to your own 312-record finding, and invoke NDPA 2023 Section 40 with the 72-hour NDPC duty. To push higher you would name Section 41 too, the duty to notify the affected data subjects when the risk to them is high, which clearly applies to 312 customers with exposed balances. I looked for a defensible way to round this into the high 70s and the evidence did not support it, because the missing findings and the incomplete, partly unproven exploit chain are real gaps, not presentation quibbles. The single most important fix: complete the exploit chain end to end with a verbatim PoC for every hop including the XXE payload, and correct the SQLi vector to A:N (about 9.1).
